author: reek
body: `comp-draw-node` handled five of the seven widget kinds and answered `otherwise -> 0` for `WkInput` and `WkCustom`. A widget that lays out, occupies its space and paints nothing reads as a layout bug rather than as a missing arm, which is why it survived: the tree looked right and the pixels were simply absent. This pins both arms.

author: reek
body: **The measurement is a DIFFERENCE against a baseline, and the first cut of this test got that wrong.** It rendered one tree and counted non-zero cells inside the child's bounds. Every cell in the buffer is non-zero, because the root panel fills the whole rectangle before any child paints, so that counted the panel and answered the same thing whatever the child did. Here each arm renders twice -- a root with no children, then the same root with the child -- and counts the cells that CHANGED. That is the child's own contribution and nothing else.

author: reek
body: The gauge is the calibration. It was drawn before this change, so it must register under exactly this harness; if its row ever reads `no` the harness is broken and the rows above it are answering a question nobody asked.

author: reek
body: `event-dot` is counted exactly: six by six is 36 cells, so a dot drawn at the wrong size or in the wrong place fails on the number rather than on a yes.

author: reek
body: **Fired against the arms removed** (`otherwise -> 0` restored, seed 37A7EF8E4EF603AE): `input painted` and `event-dot is 6 by 6` both go to `no` and the gauge control holds. `input inside its box` stays `yes` under that sabotage and it is worth saying why rather than counting it as a third moved row: with nothing painted both counts are zero and zero equals zero. It is meaningful only while `input painted` reads yes, which is the row it is paired with.

author: reek
body: The unknown-tag fallback is deliberately NOT asserted here. It fills its bounds with the panel style, `widget-resolve-style` gives a `WkCustom` the same panel style as its parent, and painting a colour over the same colour changes no cell. It is unobservable by difference, and a row that cannot fail is worse than an absent one.

author: reek
body: The baseline is painted once: the root alone, no children. Every arm below is the same root with one child added, so any cell that differs from this buffer was written by that child.
